steps.title: Photosynthesis
steps.body: The process by which plants make glucose using light energy, carbon dioxide and water. Oxygen is produced as a by-product.

steps.title: Photosynthesis
steps.body: takes place in the chloroplasts of plant cells. Chlorophyll (the green pigment) absorbs light energy, which is used to convert carbon dioxide and water into glucose and oxygen.

steps.title: Key points about the equation
steps.body: Light energy is required (absorbed by chlorophyll) It is an endothermic reaction (takes in energy from the surroundings) Happens in chloroplasts, which contain chlorophyll Oxygen is a by-product (not the main product)

steps.title: Limiting factor
steps.body: The factor that is at the least favourable level and therefore limits the rate of photosynthesis. At any given moment, whichever factor is in shortest supply is the limiting factor.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Write the word equation and symbol equation for photosynthesis. | Name the three limiting factors for photosynthesis and explain how each affects the rate. | Higher A lamp is moved from 10 cm to 30 cm away from a plant. By what factor does the light intensity change?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Word equation: carbon dioxide + water → glucose + oxygen. Symbol equation: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂. (Light energy is required; absorbed by chlorophyll.) | The three limiting factors are: (1) Light intensity — more light provides more energy for the reaction, increasing rate until another factor limits; (2) CO₂ concentration — more CO₂ provides more raw  | Distance triples from 10 cm to 30 cm. Light intensity ∝ 1/d². New intensity = 1/30² = 1/900. Original = 1/10² = 1/100. Factor = 100/900 = 1/9. Light intensity is reduced to one ninth.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Make sure you can write both the word and symbol equation from memory — these are frequently tested When asked about limiting factors, always identify WHICH factor is limiting and explain WHY Higher tier: learn the inverse square law (light intensity ∝ 1/d²) — if distance triples, intensity drops to 1/9th Remember: photosynthesis is ENDOTHERMIC (takes in energy), respiration is EXOTHERMIC (releases energy) When describing the pondweed practical, always mention control variables to get full marks Counting bubbles is less accurate than using an oxygen sensor — be ready to explain why (variable bubble size, missed bubbles) Don't forget that nitrates are needed to make amino acids from glucose — plants get nitrates from the soil, NOT from photosynthesis
